Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Software Engineering [NPT_4123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Compare unstructured and structured programming paradigms. Using appropriate examples,                 (5)  
  analyze how program flow and readability differ between the two approaches.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Demonstrate your understanding of software development by distinguishing between software as a (5)  
  service (SaaS) and software products and provide appropriate examples for each.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Analyze the Prototype Life Cycle Model and explain how it helps in addressing ambiguity or             (5)  
  uncertainty in software requirements during the development process.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Explain the concepts of functional and non-functional requirements in a software system. Using         (5)  
  your understanding, identify 3 functional requirements and two non-functional requirement for a  
  online shopping system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Analyze the characteristics of high-level and detailed designs, and determine the specific             (5)  
  documents that should be produced upon the completion of each design stage.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Analyze the concepts of coupling and cohesion, and describe how communicational and sequential (5)  
  cohesion are applied in software module design.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                An Online Shopping System enables users to log in, browse products, add selected items to their        (5)  
  cart, make secure payments, and receive an order confirmation. The key operations of the system  
  A)           include: user authentication, product selection, cart management, payment processing, and order  
  confirmation. Using the concepts of UML Component Diagrams, apply your understanding to  
  construct a component diagram for this system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Use your understanding of object-oriented modeling to construct a Class for a Smart Agriculture        (5)  
  
  Page #1

Monitoring System that employs IoT sensors to measure soil moisture, temperature, and humidity in  
  farmland. The system should continuously collect environmental data and analyze it to determine  
  when irrigation is required. When the soil moisture level falls below a predefined threshold, the  
  system must send an instant notification to the farmer's mobile device, alerting them to initiate  
  irrigation. All sensor readings should be stored in a central database for further analysis and  
  decision support.  
  
  Identify the main classes, their attributes, operations, and appropriate relationships  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)               Consider the following C function named sort.                                                          (5)  
  /* sort takes an integer array and sorts it in ascending order */  
  A)  
  void sort(int a[], int n){  
  int i,j;  
  $$for(i=0;i< n-1;i$$  
  $$for(j=i+1;j< n;j++)$$  
  if(a[i]>a[j])  
  {  
  $$temp=a[i];$$  
  $$a[i]=a[j];$$  
  $$a[j]=temp;$$  
  }  
  }  
  
  Explain the following  
  
  1. Decision coverage  
  2. Branch coverage  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)          Analyse the requirements and design a black-box test suite for a program that takes two strings as     (5)  
  input, identifies if the first string is a substring of the second, and displays the number of  
  occurrences. Justify how your chosen test cases achieve comprehensive coverage of the  
  program's expected behaviours and possible edge cases.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
